about: What a visitor does with the NES on its page at 6502.dbhq.uk: nothing to load, press Start, and play the bundled homebrew, Lan Master, by Shiru, which he released into the public domain (roms/README.md). The page renders these steps and the controls. Buttons are the NES pad's; the keys and the gamepad buttons that press them are the page's own map, shown beside it. NesAcceptanceTests boots the same file and checks its first picture against machines/nes/expected-frames.json, which the browser check also reads.
title: Lan Master
author: Shiru

steps.says: The machine switches on with Lan Master in it. The title fades in within a second and its music plays: the name in a blue band, PD2011 Shiru under it, and a menu of START, CODE, SFX and BGM with a blinking square by START.

steps.do: Press Start or A on the pad.
steps.says: START is chosen and the first level begins: a board of wire pieces and computers, with the level, how much is connected and the time along the top.

steps.do: Move the square with the D-pad and turn the pieces.
steps.says: A and B turn the piece under the square a quarter turn, one each way, and Select turns it half way round. Connect every computer before the time runs out.
The game pauses, with RESUME, RESTART and MAIN MENU, and the pass code of the level reached. CODE on the title screen takes a pass code, to carry on from that level later.

controls.does: moves the square on the board, and up and down in the menu
turns the piece a quarter turn; in the menu, chooses
turns the piece a quarter turn the other way; in the menu, chooses
turns the piece half way round; in the menu, moves down
pauses, with the pass code; in a menu, chooses
